advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the Complexity-baseline lock step robust to `set -e` (e.g. `python ... || status=$?` with a trap/cleanup) so the temp file is always removed and the status handoff is not dead code.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml has no `defaults:` and no `set +e` — search for 'defaults:' and 'set -euo' returned (no matches), so the GH Actions default `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` applies
With `-e`, a failing python command exits the step immediately, so `rm -f "$base_tmp"` never runs (temp-file leak) and `exit $status` is unreachable on failure
advisory.finding: The Complexity-baseline lock CI step captures `status=$?` after the python invocation and later `exit $status`, but GitHub Actions runs bash steps with `-eo pipefail` by default, so a nonzero `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` aborts the step before `status=$?`/`rm -f`/`exit $status` execute. The gate still fails closed, but the cleanup (temp-file removal) and status handoff are dead code on the failure path, leaking `$base_tmp` and making the logic misleading.
scenarios: A contributor raises a ceiling or adds an entry; the lock fails; the mktemp file is left behind on the runner and the intended `exit $status` line never executes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Guard the invocation so it does not abort under -e before cleanup, e.g. `status=0; python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock --base "$base_tmp" || status=$?; rm -f "$base_tmp"; exit $status`, or register a `trap 'rm -f "$base_tmp"' EXIT`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Remove or tighten the tautological first assertion in test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure so it actually asserts the fail-closed (`::error::`/`exit 1`) behavior.
evidence: assert "could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text or (\n    "::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text\n)
The comment `# The offending warn-and-continue string must be gone entirely.` precedes the only assertion that actually enforces the contract
assert "::warning::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock" not in text
The changed behavior is `echo "::error::..." ; exit 1` at .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:390-391 — the test never asserts the exit-1 branch, only that a warning string is absent.
Criterion (d) regression blindness: deleting the `exit 1` while removing the warning string keeps the test green.

.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:390 `echo "::error::could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock; failing closed."` — the bare phrase is present, making the left disjunct always False.
Line 157 re-asserts the identical predicate, so the compound assertion at 153-155 is redundant.
.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:389-391 changed the else branch from `::warning::` to `::error:: ... exit 1`.
No test asserts the module-size gate exits nonzero on fetch failure — the sole related test only greps for absence of a warning string.
Criterion (d) regression blindness for the specific behavior introduced by the module-size gate change.
advisory.finding: test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure's first assertion is effectively a tautology: `A not in text or B not in text` where B is the warning string that was removed, so the clause is satisfied regardless of the module-size fix and provides no real coverage; only the final `assert` line meaningfully verifies the fail-closed change.
merged_from: test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure asserts the ABSENCE of a specific '::warning::' prose string in the workflow YAML instead of the changed fail-closed behavior (that the fetch-failure branch exits nonzero). This is a change-detector: it would still pass if the `exit 1` were deleted (as long as the warning string were also gone) and would break on a behavior-preserving reword of the error message, without detecting any regression in the actual exit-code behavior the diff introduces.

The first assertion in test_module_size_lock_fails_closed_on_fetch_failure is logically redundant/dead: its left disjunct string 'could not fetch main to verify the module-size limit lock' is a substring present in the workflow (the module-size comment at line 379 and the ::error:: line at 390), so 'A not in text' is False and the `or` collapses to exactly the same predicate re-asserted on line 157. It contributes no independent check.

The module-size gate's behavior change from warn-and-continue to fail-closed (exit 1 on fetch failure) has no test that verifies the exit-code contract; the only coverage is a workflow-text prose grep. The observable fail-closed behavior (nonzero exit when main cannot be fetched) is asserted for the complexity-baseline CLI (test_cli_lock_fails_closed_on_missing_base) but never for the module-size gate this diff also changed.
scenarios: If the warn-and-continue text were reintroduced with slightly different phrasing, the first assertion would still pass, masking a regression until the final assertion catches the exact string.
